S01.written: I look at an airline punctuality table because I would quite like my flight to arrive when it says it will. Apparently, this is a statistical ambition.
S01.spoken: I look at an airline punctuality table because I would quite like my flight to arrive when it says it will. Apparently, this is a statistical ambition.

S01.written: In the published operating rankings, United and Southwest sit side by side. In 2024, their on-time rates are 78.60% and 78.57%. In 2025, both are still about seventy-eight percent, with Southwest just ahead.
S01.spoken: In the published operating rankings, United and Southwest sit side by side. In twenty twenty-four, their on-time rates are seventy-eight point six zero percent and seventy-eight point five seven percent. In twenty twenty-five, both are still about seventy-eight percent, with Southwest just ahead.

S01.written: My obvious answer is: equally punctual. But I want to know whether that apparent tie survives comparing similar trips. I'm testing United-operated and Southwest-operated flights. United Express and other codeshare operators are excluded.
S01.spoken: My obvious answer is: equally punctual. But I want to know whether that apparent tie survives comparing similar trips. I'm testing United-operated and Southwest-operated flights. United Express and other codeshare operators are excluded.

S02.written: First, “on time” needs a definition. Here, a flight succeeds if it completes without cancellation or diversion and arrives less than fifteen minutes after its own published arrival time. Exactly fifteen minutes late fails.
S02.spoken: First, “on time” needs a definition. Here, a flight succeeds if it completes without cancellation or diversion and arrives less than fifteen minutes after its own published arrival time. Exactly fifteen minutes late fails.

S02.written: A cancellation is a failure, not a flight that conveniently vanishes from the denominator. Diversions fail too. If the outcome cannot be determined, the primary score counts it as a failure and the interval allows for that uncertainty.
S02.spoken: A cancellation is a failure, not a flight that conveniently vanishes from the denominator. Diversions fail too. If the outcome cannot be determined, the primary score counts it as a failure and the interval allows for that uncertainty.

S02.written: The published national tables already retain failed scheduled services. My objection isn't that they forgot cancellations. It's that their averages describe different collections of flights.
S02.spoken: The published national tables already retain failed scheduled services. My objection isn't that they forgot cancellations. It's that their averages describe different collections of flights.

S03.written: Across all reported flights in 2023–2024, United is at 78.34% and Southwest at 77.91%. In 2025, they're at 77.65% and 77.76%. These are unadjusted all-flights rates.
S03.spoken: Across all reported flights in twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four, United is at seventy-eight point three four percent and Southwest at seventy-seven point nine one percent. In twenty twenty-five, they're at seventy-seven point six five percent and seventy-seven point seven six percent. These are unadjusted all-flights rates.

S03.written: I can count those flights perfectly and still be making an awkward comparison. One airline's average mixes its routes, airports and departure times; the other's mixes a different network.
S03.spoken: I can count those flights perfectly and still be making an awkward comparison. One airline's average mixes its routes, airports and departure times; the other's mixes a different network.

S03.written: Imagine comparing runners on different courses, then debating the stopwatch's accuracy. The stopwatch may be fine. I need a more comparable course.
S03.spoken: Imagine comparing runners on different courses, then debating the stopwatch's accuracy. The stopwatch may be fine. I need a more comparable course.

S03.written: So I restrict the question to opportunities both operators actually served. That changes the population I'm describing.
S03.spoken: So I restrict the question to opportunities both operators actually served. That changes the population I'm describing.

S04.written: My unit is a comparable cell: the same directional airport route, the same scheduled departure day, and the same two-hour departure window. Both airlines must have scheduled service in it.
S04.spoken: My unit is a comparable cell: the same directional airport route, the same scheduled departure day, and the same two-hour departure window. Both airlines must have scheduled service in it.

S04.written: For a concrete example, imagine Denver to Los Angeles on the same day, with both departures scheduled between ten in the morning and noon. This is a teaching example, not a pair of observed flight records.
S04.spoken: For a concrete example, imagine Denver to Los Angeles on the same day, with both departures scheduled between ten in the morning and noon. This is a teaching example, not a pair of observed flight records.

S04.written: Los Angeles to Denver is a different cell. Another date is different. A departure outside that window is different. I match scheduled departures, so a delay cannot move a flight into a friendlier comparison.
S04.spoken: Los Angeles to Denver is a different cell. Another date is different. A departure outside that window is different. I match scheduled departures, so a delay cannot move a flight into a friendlier comparison.

S04.written: The window makes circumstances more alike. It doesn't make them identical.
S04.spoken: The window makes circumstances more alike. It doesn't make them identical.

S05.written: Inside each cell, I calculate each operator's success rate. Then I give both operators the same cell weight, based on their combined scheduled-flight count. A busy shared cell matters more than a quiet one, equally for both sides.
S05.spoken: Inside each cell, I calculate each operator's success rate. Then I give both operators the same cell weight, based on their combined scheduled-flight count. A busy shared cell matters more than a quiet one, equally for both sides.

S05.written: The first period pools 2023–2024. I keep 2025 separate as replication, using that year's own comparable basket.
S05.spoken: The first period pools twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four. I keep twenty twenty-five separate as replication, using that year's own comparable basket.

S05.written: The decision line is two percentage points: one extra timely completion per fifty scheduled flights. United's whole uncertainty interval must sit above it.
S05.spoken: The decision line is two percentage points: one extra timely completion per fifty scheduled flights. United's whole uncertainty interval must sit above it.

S05.written: This single-pair rule was fixed after an exploratory pilot and a failed simulation gate, before confirmation outcomes. I don't get to move the line after seeing the answer.
S05.spoken: This single-pair rule was fixed after an exploratory pilot and a failed simulation gate, before confirmation outcomes. I don't get to move the line after seeing the answer.

S06.written: Before opening any 2023–2025 flight outcomes, I tested the uncertainty procedure on simulated outcomes with known answers. Two earlier simulation checks failed. The interval was redesigned after those failures, while the real outcomes stayed closed.
S06.spoken: Before opening any twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-five flight outcomes, I tested the uncertainty procedure on simulated outcomes with known answers. Two earlier simulation checks failed. The interval was redesigned after those failures, while the real outcomes stayed closed.

S06.written: The revised method keeps whole stretches of calendar days together across the network, because disruption can travel across airports and persist over time.
S06.spoken: The revised method keeps whole stretches of calendar days together across the network, because disruption can travel across airports and persist over time.

S06.written: Fresh simulation runs and a separate validation bank then passed the specified checks. That is evidence under those simulated conditions, not a guarantee for every possible disruption.
S06.spoken: Fresh simulation runs and a separate validation bank then passed the specified checks. That is evidence under those simulated conditions, not a guarantee for every possible disruption.

S06.written: I want the failed checks in the film. A redesigned test has a history, and that history belongs beside its result.
S06.spoken: I want the failed checks in the film. A redesigned test has a history, and that history belongs beside its result.

S07.written: In the comparable 2023–2024 basket, United's common-weighted timely-completion rate is 79.75%; Southwest's is 73.48%.
S07.spoken: In the comparable twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four basket, United's common-weighted timely-completion rate is seventy-nine point seven five percent; Southwest's is seventy-three point four eight percent.

S07.written: The gap is 6.3 percentage points for United. The nominal 99% uncertainty envelope runs from 4.60 to 7.94 points. The entire envelope clears the two-point line.
S07.spoken: The gap is six point three percentage points for United. The nominal ninety-nine percent uncertainty envelope runs from four point six zero to seven point nine four points. The entire envelope clears the two-point line.

S07.written: The permitted verdict is: United advantage above two points.
S07.spoken: The permitted verdict is: United advantage above two points.

S07.written: Those bars describe variability under repeated outcomes and calendar disruptions on the fixed schedules. They aren't uncertainty about how many historical flights I counted, or a promise about my next ticket.
S07.spoken: Those bars describe variability under repeated outcomes and calendar disruptions on the fixed schedules. They aren't uncertainty about how many historical flights I counted, or a promise about my next ticket.

S08.written: I sealed that first result before opening the 2025 outcomes. The second period gets its own test; it cannot rewrite the first.
S08.spoken: I sealed that first result before opening the twenty twenty-five outcomes. The second period gets its own test; it cannot rewrite the first.

S08.written: In 2025, the United advantage is 8.2 points. Its nominal 99% envelope runs from 5.31 to 11.00. Again, the whole interval is above two points.
S08.spoken: In twenty twenty-five, the United advantage is eight point two points. Its nominal ninety-nine percent envelope runs from five point three one to eleven point zero zero. Again, the whole interval is above two points.

S08.written: The same decisive label repeats: replicated.
S08.spoken: The same decisive label repeats: replicated.

S08.written: That doesn't mean the two periods had identical routes or schedules. And it isn't a repeated reversal of the national ranking: United already led nationally in 2023 and 2024. The important finding is a larger difference within these comparable baskets than the national near-tie suggests.
S08.spoken: That doesn't mean the two periods had identical routes or schedules. And it isn't a repeated reversal of the national ranking: United already led nationally in twenty twenty-three and twenty twenty-four. The important finding is a larger difference within these comparable baskets than the national near-tie suggests.

S09.written: I also checked nearby choices specified before the outcomes. With one-hour or four-hour windows, the estimated United gaps stay in the same direction in both periods.
S09.spoken: I also checked nearby choices specified before the outcomes. With one-hour or four-hour windows, the estimated United gaps stay in the same direction in both periods.

S09.written: Matching reciprocal nearest departures within thirty minutes gives gaps of 6.7 and 9.1 points.
S09.spoken: Matching reciprocal nearest departures within thirty minutes gives gaps of six point seven and nine point one points.

S09.written: Those are descriptive sensitivity checks. They cannot replace the registered result, and consistency doesn't make this a result about every flight.
S09.spoken: Those are descriptive sensitivity checks. They cannot replace the registered result, and consistency doesn't make this a result about every flight.

S09.written: Now I need to ask a different question: what does arriving on time actually reward? Both airlines are being judged against the timetable they publish themselves. That deserves a closer look.
S09.spoken: Now I need to ask a different question: what does arriving on time actually reward? Both airlines are being judged against the timetable they publish themselves. That deserves a closer look.

S10.written: These next checks are exploratory: post-hoc, not registered. United schedules about 4.5 minutes longer on the shared basket in both periods. But its actual gate-to-gate duration is longer too: about 4.8 minutes in 2023–2024 and 6.2 in 2025, among cells with completed observations for both operators. Longer schedules don't establish deliberate padding.
S10.spoken: These next checks are exploratory: post-hoc, not registered. United schedules about four point five minutes longer on the shared basket in both periods. But its actual gate-to-gate duration is longer too: about four point eight minutes in twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four and six point two in twenty twenty-five, among cells with completed observations for both operators. Longer schedules don't establish deliberate padding.

S10.written: I then give both airlines a shared elapsed-time allowance from their own scheduled departure, using the midpoint of their cell-average scheduled durations and the same fifteen-minute cutoff. This isn't one wall-clock arrival deadline.
S10.spoken: I then give both airlines a shared elapsed-time allowance from their own scheduled departure, using the midpoint of their cell-average scheduled durations and the same fifteen-minute cutoff. This isn't one wall-clock arrival deadline.

S10.written: The United gaps shrink to 2.6 and 4.3 points. That shows deadline sensitivity; it doesn't tell me how much padding caused. These exploratory results do not inherit the registered verdict.
S10.spoken: The United gaps shrink to two point six and four point three points. That shows deadline sensitivity; it doesn't tell me how much padding caused. These exploratory results do not inherit the registered verdict.

S11.written: I can also look at leaving, before an arrival deadline enters the story. This departure check is exploratory too.
S11.spoken: I can also look at leaving, before an arrival deadline enters the story. This departure check is exploratory too.

S11.written: Southwest has noncancelled departures fifteen minutes or more late about 10.1 points more often in 2023–2024 and 13.1 points more often in 2025. The denominator is all scheduled flights; a cancellation isn't counted as an observed late departure.
S11.spoken: Southwest has noncancelled departures fifteen minutes or more late about ten point one points more often in twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four and thirteen point one points more often in twenty twenty-five. The denominator is all scheduled flights; a cancellation isn't counted as an observed late departure.

S11.written: Including cancellations as failures in a timely-departure score gives United advantages of 9.9 and 13.3 points.
S11.spoken: Including cancellations as failures in a timely-departure score gives United advantages of nine point nine and thirteen point three points.

S11.written: Arrival padding cannot mechanically explain departure delays. But scheduled departure choices and operating circumstances still travel with the airline. I haven't isolated a cause, or the effect of choosing United for a ticket.
S11.spoken: Arrival padding cannot mechanically explain departure delays. But scheduled departure choices and operating circumstances still travel with the airline. I haven't isolated a cause, or the effect of choosing United for a ticket.

S12.written: Finally, this is a small overlap: about eleven to twelve percent of United-operated schedules and six percent of Southwest's. United Express is excluded.
S12.spoken: Finally, this is a small overlap: about eleven to twelve percent of United-operated schedules and six percent of Southwest's. United Express is excluded.

S12.written: An exploratory concentration check finds about eighty percent of the comparison weight touches Denver.
S12.spoken: An exploratory concentration check finds about eighty percent of the comparison weight touches Denver.

S12.written: Another exploratory, post-hoc check splits scheduled departures by local time. Before ten in the morning, the gaps are near zero: minus 0.4 and plus 1.4 points. From four in the afternoon onward, they're 11.7 and 12.9. The overall average conceals a very different day.
S12.spoken: Another exploratory, post-hoc check splits scheduled departures by local time. Before ten in the morning, the gaps are near zero: minus zero point four and plus one point four points. From four in the afternoon onward, they're eleven point seven and twelve point nine. The overall average conceals a very different day.

S12.written: I can say United kept its own timetable more often on these comparable operating services, with a result that replicated. I can't turn that into faster travel, a causal explanation, rebooking outcomes, a recommendation or a best-airline ranking.
S12.spoken: I can say United kept its own timetable more often on these comparable operating services, with a result that replicated. I can't turn that into faster travel, a causal explanation, rebooking outcomes, a recommendation or a best-airline ranking.

S12.written: Next time I see a national tie, I want to ask which flights went into it, and whose deadline they had to meet.
S12.spoken: Next time I see a national tie, I want to ask which flights went into it, and whose deadline they had to meet.

Short A.written: United and Southwest look almost tied in national punctuality tables. I wanted to compare similar flights instead.
Short A.spoken: United and Southwest look almost tied in national punctuality tables. I wanted to compare similar flights instead.

Short A.written: I matched the same directional route, scheduled day and two-hour departure window. This covers United-operated and Southwest-operated domestic nonstop services, excluding United Express.
Short A.spoken: I matched the same directional route, scheduled day and two-hour departure window. This covers United-operated and Southwest-operated domestic nonstop services, excluding United Express.

Short A.written: Against each airline's own arrival timetable, United leads by 6.3 points in 2023–2024 and 8.2 in 2025. Both whole nominal 99% uncertainty envelopes clear the two-point line: replicated. Cancellations count as failures.
Short A.spoken: Against each airline's own arrival timetable, United leads by six point three points in twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four and eight point two in twenty twenty-five. Both whole nominal ninety-nine percent uncertainty envelopes clear the two-point line: replicated. Cancellations count as failures.

Short A.written: This is a small, Denver-heavy overlap, not a best-airline ranking. A shared-deadline check shrinks the gaps. I found a comparable-service difference, not advice about which ticket to buy.
Short A.spoken: This is a small, Denver-heavy overlap, not a best-airline ranking. A shared-deadline check shrinks the gaps. I found a comparable-service difference, not advice about which ticket to buy.

Short B.written: “On time” depends on whose timetable I use. In an exploratory check of comparable United-operated and Southwest-operated flights, United schedules about 4.5 minutes longer. It also actually takes longer: 4.8 minutes in 2023–2024 and 6.2 in 2025, on cells with completed flights from both operators. United Express is excluded.
Short B.spoken: “On time” depends on whose timetable I use. In an exploratory check of comparable United-operated and Southwest-operated flights, United schedules about four point five minutes longer. It also actually takes longer: four point eight minutes in twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four and six point two in twenty twenty-five, on cells with completed flights from both operators. United Express is excluded.

Short B.written: With a shared elapsed-time allowance from each scheduled departure, United's arrival advantages shrink to 2.6 and 4.3 points. Cancellations still fail.
Short B.spoken: With a shared elapsed-time allowance from each scheduled departure, United's arrival advantages shrink to two point six and four point three points. Cancellations still fail.

Short B.written: Southwest also leaves fifteen-plus minutes late more often; arrival padding can't mechanically explain departures.
Short B.spoken: Southwest also leaves fifteen-plus minutes late more often; arrival padding can't mechanically explain departures.

Short B.written: These are post-hoc checks, not registered verdicts. They show why the deadline matters without identifying deliberate padding or telling me which airline to book.
Short B.spoken: These are post-hoc checks, not registered verdicts. They show why the deadline matters without identifying deliberate padding or telling me which airline to book.

Short C.written: An average can hide a clock. I made an exploratory, post-hoc time-of-day check on comparable United-operated and Southwest-operated domestic nonstop flights. United Express is excluded; cancellations fail, and each operator is judged against its own timetable.
Short C.spoken: An average can hide a clock. I made an exploratory, post-hoc time-of-day check on comparable United-operated and Southwest-operated domestic nonstop flights. United Express is excluded; cancellations fail, and each operator is judged against its own timetable.

Short C.written: Before ten in the morning, United's gaps are near zero: minus 0.4 points in 2023–2024, plus 1.4 in 2025. From four in the afternoon onward, they're 11.7 and 12.9 points.
Short C.spoken: Before ten in the morning, United's gaps are near zero: minus zero point four points in twenty twenty-three to twenty twenty-four, plus one point four in twenty twenty-five. From four in the afternoon onward, they're eleven point seven and twelve point nine points.

Short C.written: That's local scheduled departure time, within the same route, day and window comparisons. About eighty percent of the weight touches Denver.
Short C.spoken: That's local scheduled departure time, within the same route, day and window comparisons. About eighty percent of the weight touches Denver.

Short C.written: This pattern isn't a registered verdict, a causal explanation or a morning-flight recommendation. It tells me to ask what an average has hidden.
Short C.spoken: This pattern isn't a registered verdict, a causal explanation or a morning-flight recommendation. It tells me to ask what an average has hidden.
